faq.q: Which is bigger, the Mangusta 80 or Azimut 58?
faq.a: The Mangusta 80 is larger at 24 metres, compared to the Azimut 58 at 17.6 metres. Both can carry up to 12 passengers, but the Mangusta offers more deck space and a sportier profile.

faq.q: Does the Azimut 58 have a flybridge?
faq.a: Yes, the Azimut 58 Flybridge features a spacious flybridge with seating, sun pads, and a hardtop. It’s perfect for panoramic views and alfresco dining while cruising the Marbella coast.

faq.q: How much does it cost to charter the Mangusta 80 in Marbella?
faq.a: The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter. This includes a jet ski, licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT. Longer durations are available on request.

faq.q: Can I charter the Azimut 58 for a half day?
faq.a: Yes, half-day and full-day charters are available. Pricing is on request via WhatsApp. Contact us for a custom quote based on your itinerary and group size.

faq.q: Which yacht is better for a party group?
faq.a: The Mangusta 80 offers a more open, party-friendly layout with a large aft deck and sunbathing areas. The Azimut 58 is more refined, with a flybridge for socialising and a more enclosed salon.

faq.q: Do both yachts depart from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Yes, both the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella’s famous marina. You can easily reach it from the Golden Mile, Marbella centre, or nearby resorts.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price for both yachts?
faq.a: Both include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). The Mangusta 80 also includes a jet ski.

faq.q: Which yacht is better for a family with children?
faq.a: The Azimut 58, with its flybridge and enclosed salon, offers more sheltered space for children. The Mangusta 80 is more open and better suited to active families who enjoy water toys.

data.body_html:
Choosing between the Mangusta 80 vs Azimut 58 in Marbella comes down to style, space, and budget. Both yachts depart from Puerto Banús and carry up to 12 passengers, but they offer very different experiences. The Mangusta 80 is a 24-metre open sport yacht with a jet ski included, while the Azimut 58 Flybridge provides a more traditional flybridge layout with panoramic lounging. This comparison breaks down the key differences so you can book the right boat for your day on the Costa del Sol.

Size and Layout

The Mangusta 80 measures 24 metres (78 feet) and features a wide, open-plan deck with a large sunbathing area aft and a spacious cockpit. Its design prioritises socialising and sunbathing. The Azimut 58 Flybridge is 17.6 metres (58 feet), with a flybridge that offers elevated seating, a wet bar, and sun pads. Below, the Azimut has a more enclosed salon with air conditioning, making it comfortable in the heat of summer. Both yachts have a beam that provides stability, but the Mangusta feels more expansive outdoors.

Capacity and Comfort

Both yachts are certified for up to 12 passengers, but the Mangusta 80 can feel more crowded if everyone wants sunbeds. The Azimut 58’s flybridge and lower deck split the group naturally, offering more intimate corners. For a party atmosphere, the Mangusta’s open layout works better. For a relaxed cruise with dining, the Azimut’s flybridge is ideal. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT.

Performance and Onboard Experience

The Mangusta 80 is powered by twin engines that deliver a thrilling ride, reaching cruising speeds around 30 knots. It’s a sport yacht that feels fast and agile. The Azimut 58, while still powerful, is more about cruising comfort. Its flybridge offers 360-degree views of the Marbella coastline, from La Concha to the mountains. Both yachts are equipped with sound systems and basic water toys, but the Mangusta 80 charter includes a jet ski – a major perk for watersports enthusiasts.

Pricing and Value

The Mangusta 80 is priced from €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter, with the jet ski included. The Azimut 58’s pricing is on request via WhatsApp, but typically falls in a similar or slightly lower range depending on season and demand. For groups wanting a premium, sporty experience with a free jet ski, the Mangusta offers clear value. For those who prefer a more traditional, flybridge-style yacht, the Azimut 58 is an excellent choice. All prices include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT.

Best Use Cases

  • Mangusta 80: Best for parties, watersports lovers, and groups wanting a sporty, open-air experience. Includes jet ski.
  • Azimut 58: Ideal for families, couples, or those seeking a refined cruise with a flybridge for lounging and dining.

Where You Can Cruise

Both yachts depart from Puerto Banús. Popular itineraries include cruising to Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés for swimming, or heading west to Estepona and Sotogrande. You can also anchor near the Golden Mile for a view of Marbella’s iconic skyline. Your skipper will tailor the route to your preferences.

How to Book

Ready to compare Marbella yacht charters? For the Mangusta 80, you can book directly at the fixed rate of €4,719 for 4 hours. For the Azimut 58, contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote. Both yachts are available for half-day, full-day, and sunset charters. We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance, especially during high season (June–September).

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is bigger, the Mangusta 80 or Azimut 58?

The Mangusta 80 is larger at 24 metres, compared to the Azimut 58 at 17.6 metres. Both can carry up to 12 passengers, but the Mangusta offers more deck space and a sportier profile.

Does the Azimut 58 have a flybridge?

Yes, the Azimut 58 Flybridge features a spacious flybridge with seating, sun pads, and a hardtop. It’s perfect for panoramic views and alfresco dining while cruising the Marbella coast.

The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter. This includes a jet ski, licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT. Longer durations are available on request.

Can I charter the Azimut 58 for a half day?

Yes, half-day and full-day charters are available. Pricing is on request via WhatsApp. Contact us for a custom quote based on your itinerary and group size.

Which yacht is better for a party group?

The Mangusta 80 offers a more open, party-friendly layout with a large aft deck and sunbathing areas. The Azimut 58 is more refined, with a flybridge for socialising and a more enclosed salon.

Do both yachts depart from Puerto Banús?

Yes, both the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella’s famous marina. You can easily reach it from the Golden Mile, Marbella centre, or nearby resorts.

What is included in the charter price for both yachts?

Both include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). The Mangusta 80 also includes a jet ski.

Which yacht is better for a family with children?

The Azimut 58, with its flybridge and enclosed salon, offers more sheltered space for children. The Mangusta 80 is more open and better suited to active families who enjoy water toys.
